- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.05) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is rising; adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–3% for days following a peak.
- When sentiment history shows increasing negativity (e.g., 0.00 → 0.00 → 0.00 → 0.00), model tends to ignore downward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.
